title: Always Use Proper Types
overview: Using proper types improves code safety and readability. Avoid using unnecessary any types because they remove TypeScript benefits.

example.title: Avoid Any

title: Prefer Interfaces and Type Aliases
overview: Interfaces and type aliases help create reusable structures for objects, API responses, and application data.

title: Enable Strict Mode
overview: Strict mode enables advanced type checking and helps identify potential issues during development.

title: Avoid Duplicate Types
overview: Reusable types should be created in separate files and shared across the application instead of rewriting the same structures.

title: TypeScript Project Organization
overview: A well-organized TypeScript project separates components, types, services, hooks, and utilities for better maintainability.

example.title: Project Structure
example.content:
src
 ├── components
 ├── screens
 ├── hooks
 ├── types
 └── services

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned important TypeScript practices including proper typing, reusable structures, strict mode, organization, and maintainable coding patterns.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
